record.paper_title: Enabling and Emerging Technologies for Social Distancing: A Comprehensive Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can novel scheduling and optimization algorithms in operations research use social distancing itself as a performance metric or design parameter across workforce scheduling, health appointment scheduling, home healthcare routing, traffic control, and online-service optimization while preserving acceptable quality of service?

evidence.quote: Nevertheless, except for the home healthcare service scenario, the existing techniques’ objectives do not align with the objectives of social distancing.
Therefore, developing novel optimization/scheduling algorithms in operations research and adopting social distancing as a new performance metric or design parameter is very much desirable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Develop a unified framework of optimization and scheduling algorithms in operations research that incorporates physical social distancing as an explicit performance metric or design parameter, alongside traditional quality-of-service objectives. Concretely, formulate and solve the following classes of problems so that a quantitative measure of social distancing (e.g., expected pairwise spatial separation, maximum simultaneous occupancy of a region, or probability of close contact below a threshold distance d within a time window τ) is either part of the objective function or appears as a hard/soft constraint:

1. Workforce scheduling: Given a set of workers, shifts, tasks, and a workspace partitioned into zones with capacity limits, assign workers to shifts and zones to optimize a weighted combination of productivity and a social-distancing metric (e.g., minimizing the number of worker-pairs whose spatiotemporal trajectories come within distance d).

2. Health appointment scheduling: Given patient arrivals, service-time distributions, and waiting-room geometry, design appointment times that minimize patient waiting time and provider idle time subject to constraints bounding the expected and maximum number of co-present patients within distance d.

3. Home healthcare routing: Given caregivers, patients with time windows, and travel networks, design vehicle/visit schedules that minimize travel cost and maximize service coverage while limiting caregiver-caregiver and caregiver-patient cumulative close-contact exposure.

4. Traffic control: Given a road or pedestrian network with demand, design signal timings and routing policies that optimize throughput and delay while bounding the density of agents in any spatial cell so that pairwise distances stay above d with high probability.

5. Online-service optimization: For services with physical fulfillment (deliveries, queues, retail visits), design assignment and dispatch policies that optimize service-level objectives subject to social-distancing constraints on workers and customers.

For each class, (a) give a precise mathematical formulation including the social-distancing metric, (b) characterize the computational complexity, and (c) provide algorithms (exact, approximation, or online) with provable guarantees on both the quality-of-service objective and the social-distancing metric.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a broad research direction calling for new optimization/scheduling formulations that use social distancing as an explicit objective or constraint. While individual works since 2020 (e.g., on socially-distanced appointment scheduling, distancing-aware vehicle routing, and pandemic-aware workforce scheduling) have addressed pieces of the problem, no unified framework with provable guarantees across all five settings is established. The overall program remains open.

status_evidence.title: Appointment scheduling under social distancing
status_evidence.snippet: Studies appointment scheduling with distancing constraints; addresses one sub-problem only.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists on individual sub-problems but no unified framework.
